text:
Maya: heads-up - Sprout POC reporting intermittent slow first-token latency after a 2-min burst test, started ~08:40 PT. They see p50 jump from ~180ms to 600-1.1s.
Victor: are they on hosted or dedicated? any special config?
Maya: hosted, trial org. They followed our presales note and turned on prefill with small batch window.
Lina: do we have the exact runtime/version? ops-bot?
ops-bot: deploy `runtime-v2.13.0` active in `us-east-1` since 08:15 PT. No cluster-level alarms.
Ravi: what's their prefill config and concurrency? small window + concurrency is a classic KV thrash.
Maya: config pasted by customer: `prefill: true, prefill_batch_window_ms: 150, prefill_strict_sequencing: false`, concurrency ~10, avg prompt 140 tokens, model `redwood-2-8b-quant`.
Tess: any 429s observed?
Maya: they saw some 429 spikes during the burst, then a few minutes later latency spiking.
Victor: please run the session diagnostics. use `curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/diag/session/<sid>?fields=queue,kvcache,backend` and paste the excerpt.
Maya: customer returned this snippet: `queue_wait_ms: 420, kvcache_hit: false, backend_ms: 95, rate_limit_remaining: 86`.
Lina: kvcache_hit false + high queue_wait is our likely culprit. Small prefill window causes many small KV writes that race with reads across shards. Reads miss and force backend work.
Ravi: mitigation options (ranked): 1) temporary disable prefill to check baseline; 2) increase batch window to 800-1000ms; 3) enable strict sequencing to serialize prefill per session (more stable but increases prefill latency).
Tess: customer worried about demo impact and asked if we can provide a credit if POC days are affected. I can draft a goodwill credit offer contingent on us reproducing and applying fix.
Victor: short test plan: A) disable prefill, rerun the same burst pattern for 3 mins, collect p50/p95 and watch for 429s. B) if stable, re-enable with `prefill_batch_window_ms=1000` and observe for 30 min with us watching per-shard queue metrics.
Maya: customer tried disabling prefill quickly and reported p50 ~ 210ms and no 429s during a 5-min rerun.
Lina: that confirms prefill interaction. Recommend controlled re-enable tomorrow during their demo window with us in the call.
Ravi: I'll pull per-shard queue metrics and KV miss-rate dashboards. also check if any auto-throttles fired (`x-ratelimit-remaining` low).
ops-bot: ticket #6022 updated: "Disabled prefill temporarily; p50 improved to ~210ms. Plan controlled re-enable with increased batch window. Monitor kvcache hit-rate."
Tess: I'll propose the following email to the customer: summarize the experiment, commit to a guided re-enable with us monitoring, and offer a 1-day usage credit if instability persists after config change.
Victor: include the exact API patch snippet we want them to apply and the diag command; makes it easy for them.
Lina: API snippet for the email: ```PATCH /v1/projects/<proj>/settings
{ "prefill": { "enabled": true, "prefill_batch_window_ms": 1000, "prefill_strict_sequencing": false } }```
Maya: also include the diag curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/diag/session/<sid>?fields=queue,kvcache,rate`
Ravi: follow-ups for the team: - monitor kvcache hit-rate during re-enable - capture per-shard queue_length and queue_wait_ms - watch for 429s and note `x-ratelimit-*` headers - if unstable, switch to strict_sequencing and retest
Tess: sales ops, please approve provisional credit wording; I'll drop it into the deal thread.
ops-bot: note added to ticket #6022: "Customer to perform controlled re-enable TOM 09:00 PT. Team on watch. Credit pledge pending sales ops approval."
Victor: thanks all. Maya, can you schedule the 09:00 PT join link and invite Lina + Ravi?
Maya: invite sent. Customer confirmed demo shift to 09:30 PT to follow our window.
Lina: on the call we'll stream the shard queues and KV miss graphs; bring a short script to tail queue_wait_ms per shard.
Ravi: I'll also prepare a short rollback runbook in case the re-enable causes regressions.
Maya: will close the loop after the session with a short postmortem and exact metrics. :thumbsup:
